subject: Renewal options: price-hold, surge credits, and commit split
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwo od.ai>
To: Olivia Harper <olivia.harper@novum.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal options: price-hold, surge credits, and commit split

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. We know Novum is gearing up for product launch next year and want to make sure pricing and capacity don't slow you down. Based on the usage patterns you shared, I put together three practical renewal paths that balance unit economics and operational certainty:

1) 12-month Tiered Commit + 6-month price-hold
   - 25% commit increase (to cover burst during launch)
   - 6-month price-hold at current effective rate
   - Standard true-up at quarter end

2) 24-month Split Commit (Baseline + Growth Tranche)
   - Lower baseline commit (protects budget) + growth tranche that auto-applies when monthly usage exceeds baseline
   - One-time surge credit of $40k to smooth initial months

3) Short-term Bridge + Consumption Guard (transitional offer)
   - 6-month bridge with usage-based overage capped at a fixed rate
   - Option to convert to a multi-year commit with conversion credits

Attached: a draft SOW (Novum_SOW_draft_v3.pdf) and your Q3 usage export for reference (novum_usage_Q3.csv).

If Procurement prefers price-hold over a larger commit, option (1) should be easiest to approve. If you want runway but minimal up-front commitment, option (2) gives capacity uplift with a safety net.

Two asks:
- Let me know which option you want to explore in detail (I can turn one into a marked-up term sheet).
- If Procurement needs a one-page summary for approval, I can prepare it by Friday.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192
From: Olivia Harper <olivia.harper@novum.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novum AI Procurement <procurement@novum.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options: price-hold, surge credits, and commit split

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear options. Quick notes from our side: 

- Procurement is inclined toward a price-hold (option 1) because our FTEs want predictable unit cost for the first half of 2027.
- The team is also asking for an acceleration credit to offset the first two months of elevated usage post-launch — that’s non-negotiable for finance to sign off.
- We're interested in a hybrid: start with option 1 plus a smaller baseline and a modest growth tranche (somewhere between options 1 and 2).

Questions:
1) Can the price-hold be extended to 9 months if we commit to a 30% increase?
2) Can you structure the surge credit as a one-time invoice credit instead of a service credit? Our procurement team prefers credits on invoices for audit traceability.

Looping in Procurement (procurement@novum.ai) — they’ll share the approval checklist.

Thanks,
Olivia Harper
VP Product, Novum AI
olivia.harper@novum.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Harper <olivia.harper@novum.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options: price-hold, surge credits, and commit split

Hi Olivia —

Great feedback — happy to do a hybrid. Quick answers: 

1) Price-hold extension: Yes, we can extend to 9 months with a 30% commit increase. I’ll mark that as Variant A in the term sheet.
2) Surge credit format: We can issue a one-time invoice credit up to $45k (to cover a bit more than you requested) rather than applying as a service-side credit.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll share a marked-up SOW and a short executive summary for Procurement.
- Marissa — can you confirm finance sign-off on a $45k invoice credit and the mechanics for applying it? We might need a short approval for billing.
- Rishi — if Novum wants the lower baseline + growth tranche we should model latency/cost at both baseline and growth volumes; can you run an ops estimate?

If this looks OK I can send a formal term sheet and DocuSign link by EOD tomorrow.

Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options: price-hold, surge credits, and commit split

Karthik / Rishi —

Billing confirms we can apply a one-time invoice credit of up to $45,000. A couple of operational notes:

- The credit will be applied to the first post-renewal invoice that includes overage charges (we'll tag it with the Novum deal id).
- For a 9-month price-hold tied to a 30% commit uplift, Finance needs an internal approval path: an approval email chain from EVP-Sales (I can kick this off).
- Rishi, please model expected token throughput at baseline vs growth tranche and flag any GPU/throughput concerns — we should make sure our Dedicated pools can handle a sustained 40% spike.

Karthik — once Rishi provides the ops estimate, I’ll prepare a one-page approval memo and route it to EVP-Sales. If all good, go ahead and prepare the DocuSign with the Variant A numbers and the invoice-credit clause.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
